categories.blurb: 第一個問題決定對方會給你罐頭答案還是真話。
把抽象答案逼成一個真實故事。
對方講完了，再往下一層。台灣人通常在這裡停。
問什麼行不通，比問什麼有用更能挖到真東西。
把觀念逼成「我明天可以做什麼」。
把對方講的整理回去讓他確認。
怎麼結束一個話題而不突兀。

questions.q: Let me set the stage for the conversation that we're going to have today.
questions.zh: 我先把今天這場對話的背景鋪一下。
questions.why: 開場先宣告「我要鋪背景」，等於當場跟對方買下三十秒的獨白時間，他知道現在不用急著接話。省掉「以為你問完了、其實還沒」的搶拍尷尬。
questions.pattern: Let me set the stage for [the conversation] that we're going to have [today].
questions.episode: Aishwarya Naresh Reganti + Kiriti Badam

questions.q: So, let's start with just the basics.
questions.zh: 那我們就從最基本的開始。
questions.why: just the basics 把起跑線壓到最低，替專家免除「講太淺很掉價」的顧慮，他才願意從頭講。同一句話也替聽眾建立共同背景。
questions.pattern: So, let's start with just [the basics].
questions.episode: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)

questions.q: I want to start with a spicy question.
questions.zh: 我想用一個比較嗆的問題開場。
questions.why: 先幫問題貼上 spicy 的標籤，等於預告「這題不客氣」。對方有了心理準備就不會覺得被伏擊，反而等於被授權可以直說。
questions.pattern: I want to start with a [spicy] question.
questions.episode: Boris Cherny

questions.q: There's so much I want to talk to you about, but I want to start with a warm and fuzzy question.
questions.zh: 想跟你聊的東西太多了，不過我想先從一個溫馨一點的問題開始。
questions.why: 前半句先承認「題目很多」，讓對方知道第一題只是起點不是全部，不必把話一次講完；後半句用 warm and fuzzy 定調，把第一題的壓力降到最低。
questions.pattern: There's so much I want to talk to you about, but I want to start with [a warm and fuzzy question].
questions.episode: Inside Canva: Coaches not managers, giving away your Legos, and running profitably | Cameron Adams (co-founder and CPO)

questions.q: I want to use this conversation to basically help people understand this space deeply, but let's start with the basics.
questions.zh: 我想用這場對話讓大家真正搞懂這個領域，不過我們先從基本的開始。
questions.why: 一句話同時交代整場的目標（深入）跟這一刻的位置（從基本開始）。對方知道要往深講，但現在還不用跳到深水區。
questions.pattern: I want to use this conversation to basically help people understand [X] deeply, but let's start with the basics.
questions.episode: Why AI evals are the hottest new skill for product builders | Hamel Husain & Shreya Shankar (creators of the #1 eval course)

questions.q: I want to start with a phrase that came up again and again when I ask people what to talk to you about from your colleagues, and this phrase is conscious leadership.
questions.zh: 我想從一個詞開始。我問你同事該跟你聊什麼的時候，這個詞一直重複出現——conscious leadership。
questions.why: 把題目的來源掛在第三方身上（同事、反覆出現），問題就不是你的好奇而是既成事實，對方很難迴避。關鍵詞留到最後才丟，製造一個小懸念。
questions.pattern: I want to start with a phrase that came up again and again when I ask people [what to talk to you about], and this phrase is [X].
questions.episode: Becoming a conscious leader: Leading without fear, finding your life’s objective function, and getting better at vision and strategy | John Mark Nickels (Uber, Waymo, DoorDash)

questions.q: I want to start with just a big picture question.
questions.zh: 我想先問一個比較大方向的問題。
questions.why: big picture 這個標籤等於授權對方講抽象、講框架，不必先交代細節，也預告了細節留到後面。開場最省力的一種鋪陳。
questions.pattern: I want to start with just a [big picture] question.
questions.episode: Marc Andreessen: The real AI boom hasn’t even started yet

questions.q: I want to start by asking you a question that is on the minds of a lot of product managers is how to be less annoying as a product manager.
questions.zh: 我想先問一個很多 PM 心裡都有的問題：PM 要怎麼樣才不會那麼惹人嫌。
questions.why: 先說「這是很多人心裡的疑問」，一個可能冒犯的問題就變成群眾代表發問——對方是在回答一群人，不是被你挑釁。
questions.pattern: I want to start by asking you a question that is on the minds of a lot of [PMs], which is [X].
questions.episode: The things engineers are desperate for PMs to understand | Camille Fournier (author of “The Manager’s Path,” ex-CTO at Rent the Runway)

questions.q: I want to start with something that's very timely, something that's happening this week.
questions.zh: 我想從一件很即時的事開始，就是這禮拜正在發生的事。
questions.why: 用 timely 幫問題爭取插隊權——這題現在不問就過期了，對方不容易推說「這個晚點再談」。重複 something that's 也讓句子有節奏、順便替自己爭取想下一句的時間。
questions.pattern: I want to start with something that's very timely, something that's happening [this week].
questions.episode: Benjamin Mann

questions.q: I want to start with the elephant in the room, which I think the elephant is actually leaving the room because I think this is months ago at this point, but I'm still just really curious.
questions.zh: 我想從房間裡那頭大象開始講——雖然我覺得那頭象其實正在離場了，因為這都幾個月前的事了，但我還是很好奇。
questions.why: 先點名「大家都知道但沒人講的事」，再自己補一句「其實已經退燒」把火氣降下來，最後用 I'm still just really curious 把提問的理由歸給好奇而不是究責。
questions.pattern: I want to start with the elephant in the room, ... but I'm still just really curious.
questions.episode: Inside OpenAI | Logan Kilpatrick (head of developer relations)

questions.q: What I want to start with is to give us a little insight into how you became what you became.
questions.zh: 我想先從一件事開始：讓我們稍微了解一下，你是怎麼變成今天的你的。
questions.why: 用 give us a little insight 取代「請你自我介紹」，把題目框成分享一點內幕而不是報履歷，對方講出來的會是故事而不是條列。
questions.pattern: What I want to start with is to give us a little insight into [how you became what you became].
questions.episode: How to find hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)

questions.q: Let me start with just setting a little context, and for folks that aren't super familiar with what is a marketplace business, they hear this term marketplace company, what's the simplest way to understand what makes a company a marketplace company and a marketplace business?
questions.zh: 我先鋪一點背景。對不太熟「平台型生意」的人來說，他們聽到 marketplace company 這個詞，最簡單要怎麼理解一家公司算是 marketplace？
questions.why: 把「我不懂」外包給 folks that aren't super familiar，專家就不會覺得你在測他的程度。the simplest way to understand 又直接指定了答案的難度上限。
questions.pattern: Let me start with just setting a little context, and for folks that aren't super familiar with [X], what's the simplest way to understand [X]?
questions.episode: How marketplaces win: Liquidity, growth levers, quality, and more | Benjamin Lauzier (Lyft, Thumbtack, Reforge)

questions.q: I want to start with just trying to understand and help people understand why is it so freaking hard to build a durable, lasting consumer product and in particular a social consumer product.
questions.zh: 我想先從搞懂一件事開始，也幫大家搞懂：為什麼要做出一個能撐很久的消費型產品——尤其是社群產品——會那麼難？
questions.why: understand and help people understand 這個雙層說法把「我想知道」跟「大家想知道」綁在一起，問題就有了公共性。so freaking hard 的口語強度則在邀請對方講真話而不是官腔。
questions.pattern: I want to start with just trying to understand and help people understand why is it so hard to [X].
questions.episode: Snapchat CEO: Why distribution has become the most important moat | Evan Spiegel

questions.q: Okay, so Dylan, I want to start by just checking in on how you're doing.
questions.zh: 好，Dylan，我想先關心一下你最近好嗎。
questions.why: 先叫名字再 checking in，把第一題設定成關心而不是提問。對方通常會自己交代近況，你等於免費拿到一段脈絡當後面的引子。
questions.pattern: Okay, so [name], I want to start by just checking in on how you're doing.
questions.episode: Dylan Field live at Config: Intuition, simplicity, and the future of design

questions.q: Can you maybe make it even more concrete?
questions.zh: 可以再講得更具體一點嗎？
questions.why: 一句話把抽象打回去要細節。maybe 讓語氣不像糾正，even more 又先肯定對方剛剛已經講得不錯、只是還能再往下一層。
questions.pattern: Can you maybe make it even more concrete?
questions.episode: Unorthodox frameworks for growing your product, career, and impact | Bangaly Kaba (YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, Instacart)

questions.q: What's an example of that, just to make it more concrete for us?
questions.zh: 可以舉個例子嗎？讓我們比較具體一點。
questions.why: 先要例子，再用 just to make it more concrete for us 補上理由——把要求包成「我們需要」，對方不會解讀成「你剛剛講得不夠好」。
questions.pattern: What's an example of that, just to make it more concrete for us?
questions.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

questions.q: What's a tactical tip or two that you can suggest to a founder or product manager to help them contain the design process while also achieving these outcomes that you're describing?
questions.zh: 你會給創辦人或 PM 哪一兩個實際做得到的小訣竅，讓他們既能把設計流程收斂好、又能達到你剛講的那些結果？
questions.why: a tip or two 幫對方把答案量化成一到兩個，他就不會發散。再指定對象跟目標，答案自動變成可執行的建議而不是理念。
questions.pattern: What's a tactical tip or two that you can suggest to [a founder or PM] to help them [X] while also achieving [these outcomes]?
questions.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

questions.q: Just to leave people with a tactical piece of advice, say they are like, "Oh man, I need a coach," do you have any advice for how to find a coach?
questions.zh: 想留一個實際可用的建議給大家——假設有人心裡想「天啊我需要一個教練」，你會怎麼建議他去找？
questions.why: say they are like 後面直接演一段內心話，把抽象的「聽眾」變成一個具體的人跟具體處境。對方會針對那個處境回答，而不是講原則。
questions.pattern: Just to leave people with a tactical piece of advice, say they are like, "[內心話]," do you have any advice for how to [X]?
questions.episode: How to own your career growth and become a powerful product leader | Deb Liu, Ancestry (ex-Facebook, PayPal)

questions.q: Very tactically, what do you recommend people do?
questions.zh: 講得很實際一點，你會建議大家怎麼做？
questions.why: 把 tactically 提到句首當開關，一開口就宣告「接下來不要理論」。七個字就能把一段哲學拉回動作層。
questions.pattern: Very tactically, what do you recommend people do?
questions.episode: How to discover your superpowers, own your story, and unlock personal growth | Donna Lichaw (author of The Leader’s Journey)

questions.q: Talk about when you think about what is good taste, good judgment, what is that concretely?
questions.zh: 聊一下，你說的好品味、好判斷力，具體到底是什麼？
questions.why: 把對方用的抽象詞原封不動唸回去，再加 concretely 逼他定義。他沒辦法再用同一個詞解釋同一個詞。
questions.pattern: Talk about when you think about [抽象詞], what is that concretely?
questions.episode: OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino

questions.q: So what is a vision concretely as a document in your experience?
questions.zh: 所以以你的經驗來說，願景具體作為一份文件，長什麼樣？
questions.why: concretely as a document 幫抽象概念指定了一個實體形式——你要的不是定義，是一份可以打開來看的東西，對方只能描述真實產物。
questions.pattern: So what is [X] concretely as [a document] in your experience?
questions.episode: Crafting a compelling product vision | Ebi Atawodi (YouTube, Netflix, Uber)

questions.q: When you say data preparation, what's an example to make that real and concrete for us to understand?
questions.zh: 你說的「資料準備」，可以舉個例子讓我們具體理解嗎？
questions.why: When you say 先把對方剛用的術語隔離出來，不否定也不假裝懂。接著只要一個例子，比問「那是什麼意思」少了質疑感。
questions.pattern: When you say [術語], what's an example to make that real and concrete for us to understand?
questions.episode: Al Engineering 101 with Chip Huyen (Nvidia, Stanford, Netflix)

questions.q: What's the first step that you recommend for people to go down?
questions.zh: 你會建議大家的第一步是什麼？
questions.why: 只要 the first step、不要整套流程。對方無法丟一個大架構搪塞，聽的人也拿到一個明天就能做的動作。
questions.pattern: What's the first step that you recommend for people to go down?
questions.episode: The ultimate guide to adding a PLG motion | Hila Qu (Reforge, GitLab)

questions.q: To make that last point a little more concrete, what's an example of that?
questions.zh: 為了讓你剛剛那個點更具體一點，可以舉個例子嗎？
questions.why: that last point 精準指回剛講的那一段，對方不會整段重講。a little 又讓要求聽起來只是微調，不是打回重寫。
questions.pattern: To make that last point a little more concrete, what's an example of that?
questions.episode: Developing a growth model + marketplace growth strategy | Dan Hockenmaier (Faire, Thumbtack, Reforge)

questions.q: Do you have any tactical advice for someone that is not good at this for how to actually say something uncomfortable?
questions.zh: 對於本來就不擅長這件事的人，你有沒有什麼實際的建議，教他怎麼真的把難講的話講出口？
questions.why: 指定對象是「本來就不擅長的人」，答案的難度上限被鎖死，對方不能給只有高手做得到的建議。actually say 又把答案逼到「真的開口那一刻」。
questions.pattern: Do you have any tactical advice for someone that is not good at this for how to actually [X]?
questions.episode: Lessons from scaling Stripe | Claire Hughes Johnson (former COO of Stripe)

questions.q: Is it just in your mind you're like, "I'm going to have fun with this," or is there something tactically people can do to make something fun?
questions.zh: 這只是你心裡想「我要玩得開心一點」而已，還是說有什麼實際做法可以讓事情變好玩？
questions.why: 給一個二選一，而且故意把第一個選項寫得空泛。對方為了不落入空泛，就會選第二個並交出做法——把觀念逼成做法最有效的一招。
questions.pattern: Is it just in your mind you're like, "[心態]," or is there something tactically people can do to [X]?
questions.episode: Becoming more strategic, navigating difficult colleagues, harnessing founder mode, and more | Anneka Gupta (Chief Product Officer at Rubrik)

questions.q: How do you actually kind of tactically operationalize that?
questions.zh: 那實際上要怎麼把它變成日常在運作的東西？
questions.why: operationalize 指的是「變成制度、變成每天在跑的流程」，比 how do you do it 更難敷衍——對方必須交代誰做、多久做一次。
questions.pattern: How do you actually kind of tactically operationalize that?
questions.episode: Building a culture of excellence | David Singleton (CTO of Stripe)

questions.q: If people listening are also sold and want to build a company this way, what can they do?
questions.zh: 如果正在聽的人也被說服了，想照這個方式建一家公司，他們可以怎麼做？
questions.why: 先假設對方已經說服成功（are also sold），跳過辯論直接問下一步。他就不會再花時間補論證，而是給行動。
questions.pattern: If people listening are also sold and want to [X], what can they do?
questions.episode: Reflections on a movement | Eric Ries (creator of the Lean Startup methodology)

questions.q: Or is there a story of something where you just shipped something that shows this customer obsession to make it even more concrete for listeners?
questions.zh: 或者有沒有一個實際例子，你們出過什麼東西，能體現這種對客戶的執著，讓聽的人更有畫面？
questions.why: 要的是 story 而不是 example，對方會給時間、人物、結果，資訊密度高很多。for listeners 又把要求轉成替第三方著想。
questions.pattern: Or is there a story of something where you just [做了X] that shows [這個特質] to make it even more concrete for listeners?
questions.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

questions.q: So what I'm hearing is find a problem that can be solved, find a problem, a pain point for yourself or someone, and then end-to-end fully solve that problem.
questions.zh: 所以我聽到的是：找一個解得掉的問題，一個你自己或別人真的會痛的點，然後從頭到尾把它徹底解決。
questions.why: what I'm hearing is 把對方一長串的話濃縮成一句祈使句，等於幫他把觀點寫成標題。對方通常會接受你的版本並順著往下講。
questions.pattern: So what I'm hearing is [濃縮後的主張].
questions.episode: Building Lovable: $10M ARR in 60 days with 15 people | Anton Osika (co-founder and CEO)

questions.q: And a big part of this is distribution, essentially, breaking through the noise is what I'm hearing?
questions.zh: 所以這裡很大一塊其實是通路——重點是怎麼殺出重圍，我這樣理解對嗎？
questions.why: 把 is what I'm hearing 挪到句尾，前半句就能用肯定語氣講，聽起來像在補完對方的話；結尾才輕輕把確認權交還。比一開頭就問「你是說⋯嗎」更不打斷。
questions.pattern: [你的濃縮版本] is what I'm hearing?
questions.episode: Sequoia CEO coach: Why it’s never been easier to start a company, and never been harder to scale one | Brian Halligan (co-founder, HubSpot)

questions.q: So you intentionally set that announcement up to be controversial is what I'm hearing?
questions.zh: 所以你是刻意把那則公告弄得有爭議性的，我這樣聽對嗎？
questions.why: 把對方沒明說的動機（intentionally）講出來，再用 is what I'm hearing 收尾。他若否認會主動補說明，若默認你就拿到一個他自己不會主動講的重點。
questions.pattern: So you intentionally [做了X] is what I'm hearing?
questions.episode: “Dumbest idea I’ve heard” to $100M ARR: Inside the rise of Gamma | Grant Lee (CEO)

questions.q: Okay, let me try to reflect back some of the advice I've been hearing about how to shift a company to be successful in this new world, and let me see if I'm missing anything that you think is really important.
questions.zh: 好，我試著把剛剛聽到的建議整理回去——關於一家公司要怎麼調整才能在這個新局裡活得好——你看我有沒有漏掉什麼你覺得很重要的。
questions.why: reflect back 先宣告要複誦，再用 see if I'm missing anything 把球丟回去。最精巧的是它把「我可能聽錯」寫成「我可能漏掉」，對方補充時不必否定你。
questions.pattern: Okay, let me try to reflect back [我聽到的X], and let me see if I'm missing anything that you think is really important.
questions.episode: How we restructured Airtable’s entire org for AI | Howie Liu (co-founder and CEO)

questions.q: Just to close the loop on this advice around getting better at vision and strategy, if I were to reflect back what I'm hearing its be very self-aware about what you are not strong at, say openness.
questions.zh: 為了把「怎麼把願景跟策略做得更好」這段收個尾——如果我把聽到的整理回去，就是：要非常清楚自己哪裡不強，比方說開放性。
questions.why: close the loop 宣告這是收尾不是新問題；if I were to reflect back 用假設語氣，先替自己的複述留了退路，對方要糾正的成本趨近於零。
questions.pattern: Just to close the loop on this advice around [X], if I were to reflect back what I'm hearing it's [Y].
questions.episode: Improve strategy, influence, and decision-making by understanding your brain | Evan LaPointe (founder of CORE Sciences)

questions.q: What I'm hearing is step one is just get your kind of peer leaders aligned behind something that may not obviously be something your leaders want you to do, is that right?
questions.zh: 我聽到的是，第一步就是先把跟你平行的那些主管拉到同一邊，即使那件事表面上未必是你老闆想要你做的——是這樣嗎？
questions.why: 複述時自己加上 step one，等於把對方的話重新編號成流程；結尾補 is that right? 讓這個加工得到他的授權。
questions.pattern: What I'm hearing is step one is just [X], is that right?
questions.episode: How to sell your ideas and rise within your company | Casey Winters, Eventbrite

questions.q: So correct me if I'm wrong, but kind of the advice you're sharing is there's less opportunity in just generating tons of blog posts that just have a bunch of content.
questions.zh: 我理解錯就糾正我——你分享的建議大概是說，光是狂產一堆有內容的部落格文章，機會已經比較小了。
questions.why: correct me if I'm wrong 先把否決權交出去，你就可以放膽講一個比對方原話更銳利的版本。他若不同意會自己修正，你反而拿到更精準的說法。
questions.pattern: So correct me if I'm wrong, but kind of the advice you're sharing is [X].
questions.episode: Rethinking SEO in the age of AI | Eli Schwartz (SEO advisor, author)

questions.q: And correct me if I'm wrong, but you guys have moved away from that approach.
questions.zh: 我說錯的話糾正我——你們後來已經不走那條路了。
questions.why: 用陳述句而不是問句丟出推測，對方只要點頭或修正，比問句推進得更快；前半句是安全氣囊，讓你猜錯也不失分。
questions.pattern: And correct me if I'm wrong, but [你的推論陳述].
questions.episode: Gustav Söderström

questions.q: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this five step framework.
questions.zh: 我試著把你剛分享的整理一下，這個五步驟的架構。
questions.why: try to 讓複述變成一次嘗試而不是定論；把內容當場命名成 this five step framework，等於替對方的說法取了一個好記的名字。
questions.pattern: Let me just try to summarize what you shared, this [five step framework].
questions.episode: The power of strategic narrative | Andy Raskin

questions.q: I'm going to summarize what you just shared, which is awesome.
questions.zh: 我來把你剛剛講的整理一下，超棒的。
questions.why: 用 I'm going to 而不是 can I 直接取得發言權，後面 which is awesome 順手給個肯定，讓「我要接手講幾句」聽起來像稱讚而不是打斷。
questions.pattern: I'm going to summarize what you just shared, which is awesome.
questions.episode: Breaking the rules of growth: Why Shopify bans KPIs, optimizes for churn, prioritizes intuition, and builds toward a 100-year vision | Archie Abrams (VP Product, Head of Growth at Shopify)

questions.q: So just to summarize the audit that you do, I wrote some notes as you were talking, and maybe we can keep going from that point.
questions.zh: 我把你做的那套盤點整理一下——你在講的時候我有做筆記——然後我們也許可以從那邊接下去。
questions.why: 講出「我有做筆記」，複述就有了憑據，對方會更認真聽你的版本。最後 keep going from that point 直接把摘要當成下一段的起跑線。
questions.pattern: So just to summarize [X], I wrote some notes as you were talking, and maybe we can keep going from that point.
questions.episode: The ultimate guide to adding a PLG motion | Hila Qu (Reforge, GitLab)

questions.q: So, just to summarize, the main benefits are focuses you, lines, creates a cadence and creates a learning cycle.
questions.zh: 所以整理一下，主要的好處是讓你聚焦、對齊、建立節奏，還有形成學習循環。
questions.why: 把對方散落各處的說法收成四個並列動詞，短、平行、好記。摘要的價值就在這裡：你交回去的版本要比原話更容易被複述。
questions.pattern: So, just to summarize, the main benefits are [A], [B], [C] and [D].
questions.episode: The ultimate guide to OKRs | Christina Wodtke (Stanford)

questions.q: Okay, let me take this opportunity to try to summarize what I've learned from you so far in terms of what you guys have figured out about creating incredible product leaders.
questions.zh: 好，我趁這個機會整理一下到目前為止從你這邊學到的，關於你們在培養頂尖產品主管上摸索出來的東西。
questions.why: take this opportunity 幫這段摘要找到時機上的正當性——不是打斷，是把握機會。so far 又留了伏筆：後面還有，這只是中場整理。
questions.pattern: Okay, let me take this opportunity to try to summarize what I've learned from you so far in terms of [X].
questions.episode: How Revolut trains world-class product managers: The “local CEO” model, raw intellect over experience, and a cultural obsession with building wow products | Dmitry Zlokazov (Head of Product)

questions.q: What I'm hearing is instead of AI being baked into SaaS tools, what you're predicting here is the SaaS tools will run within Codex or Claude Code?
questions.zh: 我聽到的是，與其說 AI 被塞進 SaaS 工具裡，你在這裡預測的其實是 SaaS 工具會跑在 Codex 或 Claude Code 之內？
questions.why: 用 instead of A, what you're predicting is B 的對照句型，把對方的觀點放在一個他沒說過的對立面旁邊，輪廓一下子清楚。順便把他的說法升格成「預測」。
questions.pattern: What I'm hearing is instead of [A], what you're predicting here is [B]?
questions.episode: The AI paradox: More automation, more humans, more work | Dan Shipper

questions.q: So what you're saying is not only is there going to be this big opportunity to grow, if you don't take advantage of it, somebody in your space will.
questions.zh: 所以你的意思是，這不只是一個很大的成長機會——你不抓，同業就會抓走。
questions.why: 複述時把對方的正面主張補上反面後果（你不做、別人會做），語氣加重了，但責任還掛在對方身上，因為開頭是 what you're saying is。
questions.pattern: So what you're saying is not only [A], if you don't [X], somebody will.
questions.episode: Brian Balfour: 10 lessons on career, growth, and life

questions.q: Is there anything else along the lines of this specific type of feedback that is worth sharing before we move on to a different type of feedback?
questions.zh: 在我們換到另一種回饋之前，關於這一類回饋，還有什麼值得補充的嗎？
questions.why: 先開補充的門、再宣告換題。順序是關鍵：先問「還有嗎」等於承認這段還沒榨乾，對方就算被切斷也不會覺得被打斷。
questions.pattern: Is there anything else along the lines of [this topic] that is worth sharing before we move on to [next topic]?
questions.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

questions.q: Let me ask you one more question before we shift a whole different topic, hint, hint, AI.
questions.zh: 在我們換到一個完全不同的主題之前，我再問你一個問題——提示一下，是 AI。
questions.why: 先宣告「只剩一題」，對方會把最好的留在這一題。hint, hint 又先預告下一段主題，讓轉場變成期待而不是斷裂。
questions.pattern: Let me ask you one more question before we shift a whole different topic, hint, hint, [next topic].
questions.episode: I’ve run 75+ businesses. Here’s why you’re probably chasing the wrong idea. | Andrew Wilkinson (co‑founder of Tiny)

questions.q: One last question about the CPO role, and then I want to shift a bit to just product management and growth.
questions.zh: 關於 CPO 這個角色，最後問一題，然後我想稍微轉到產品管理跟成長。
questions.why: 「最後一題 + 下一站」塞在同一句，等於同時關門跟開門。對方回答時心裡已經在準備下一段，接得順。
questions.pattern: One last question about [X], and then I want to shift a bit to [Y].
questions.episode: How to sell your ideas and rise within your company | Casey Winters, Eventbrite

questions.q: Let me ask one more quick question on strategy and then I want to move on to career stuff.
questions.zh: 策略這塊我再快問一題，然後想接到職涯的部分。
questions.why: quick 是給對方的時間承諾，答案自然會短。跟「最後一題＋下一站」是同一招但更輕，適合已經聊很久、需要提速的時候。
questions.pattern: Let me ask one more quick question on [X] and then I want to move on to [Y].
questions.episode: Jackie Bavaro on getting better at product strategy, what exactly is strategy, PM pitfalls to avoid, advancing your career, getting into management, and much more

questions.q: One last question before we move on to the next step.
questions.zh: 在進到下一步之前，最後一個問題。
questions.why: 最短的一種收尾件。它同時做兩件事：關掉這一段的無限延伸，並提醒對方整場對話是有步驟的。
questions.pattern: One last question before we move on to the next step.
questions.episode: Customer-led growth | Georgiana Laudi (Forget The Funnel)

questions.q: Is there anything else along this thread before we move on to a different topic, anything else you want to share before we close out this chapter?
questions.zh: 這條線上還有什麼要補的嗎？在我們換題之前，還有什麼想分享的，好把這一章收起來？
questions.why: 同一個意思問兩次，第二次改用 chapter 這個比喻，把剛剛那段封裝成一個單位，暗示「講完就不回頭了」。對方通常會把壓箱的東西拿出來。
questions.pattern: Is there anything else along this thread before we move on to a different topic, anything else you want to share before we close out this chapter?
questions.episode: The creator of WordPress opens up about becoming an internet villain, why he’s taking a stand, and the future of open source | Matt Mullenweg (founder and CEO, Automattic)

questions.q: Let's shift topics and talk about product strategy.
questions.zh: 我們換個主題，來聊產品策略。
questions.why: 最乾脆的轉場：宣告換題＋直接指定新題，沒有鋪陳。上一段明顯已經收完的時候，硬轉反而俐落。
questions.pattern: Let's shift topics and talk about [X].
questions.episode: Mastering product strategy and growing as a PM | Maggie Crowley (Toast, Drift, Tripadvisor)

questions.q: Okay, let me zoom out a bit and I want to move on to a different topic.
questions.zh: 好，我拉遠一點看，然後想換到另一個主題。
questions.why: zoom out 是轉場的緩衝墊——先把鏡頭從細節拉遠，再換題就不會像硬切。中文裡我們常常直接說「那我們換個話題」，少了這一層。
questions.pattern: Okay, let me zoom out a bit and I want to move on to a different topic.
questions.episode: We replaced our sales team with 20 AI agents—here’s what happened | Jason Lemkin (SaaStr)

questions.q: Any last piece of wisdom to leave listeners with around The JOLT Effect before we move on to The Challenger Sale?
questions.zh: 在我們轉到《挑戰者銷售》之前，關於《JOLT 效應》還有什麼最後的智慧想留給聽眾的嗎？
questions.why: last piece of wisdom 把「補充」升格成「壓軸」，對方會挑最好的講而不是隨便補。leave listeners with 又把對象換成第三方——他不是在幫你收尾，是在給聽眾禮物。
questions.pattern: Any last piece of wisdom to leave listeners with around [X] before we move on to [Y]?
questions.episode: The surprising truth about what closes deals: Insights from 2.5m sales conversations | Matt Dixon (author of The Challenger Sale and The JOLT Effect)

questions.q: Let's transition to the third area I wanted to spend some time on, which is growth.
questions.zh: 我們轉到我想花點時間聊的第三塊——成長。
questions.why: 給轉場編號（the third area），聽的人立刻知道整場是有結構的、現在走到哪。編號也讓你可以合理地結束前一段，因為第二段「已經講完了」。
questions.pattern: Let's transition to the [third] area I wanted to spend some time on, which is [X].
questions.episode: Inside Linear: Building with taste, craft, and focus | Karri Saarinen (co-founder, designer, CEO)

questions.q: I have a couple of more coaching questions before we move on to a few other topics.
questions.zh: 在換到別的主題之前，我還有幾個關於教練的問題。
questions.why: 先公告「還有幾題」，對方就知道這一段還沒結束、不用把話全部塞進下一個回答，節奏會穩下來。
questions.pattern: I have a couple of more [X] questions before we move on to a few other topics.
questions.episode: How to unlock your product leadership skills | Ken Norton, Ex-Google

questions.q: I'd love to transition in to talk about investing a little bit before we get to our exciting lightning round.
questions.zh: 在進到快問快答之前，我想轉過來稍微聊一下投資。
questions.why: 一句話宣告兩層結構：下一段是投資，再下一段就要收尾了。對方能自己分配剩下的力氣。
questions.pattern: I'd love to transition in to talk about [X] a little bit before we get to [the closing segment].
questions.episode: Gokul Rajaram on designing your product development process, when and how to hire your first PM, a playbook for hiring leaders, getting ahead in you career, how to get started angel investing, more

questions.q: Is there any other ones you want to share before we move on to getting better at speaking on the spot?
questions.zh: 在我們轉到「怎麼把臨場說話練好」之前，還有其他想分享的嗎？
questions.why: 把下一段主題直接寫進轉場問句裡，對方補充的時候就會自動避開下一段會講到的東西，省掉重複。
questions.pattern: Is there any other ones you want to share before we move on to [next topic]?
questions.episode: How to speak more confidently and persuasively | Matt Abrahams (professor, podcast host, author, speaker)

questions.q: Just to close the loop here, one takeaway here that I think is really interesting is that you can fail in a job and things will be okay.
questions.zh: 這裡先把這一段收起來——我覺得有一個很有意思的收穫：你可以在一份工作上失敗，然後一切還是會沒事。
questions.why: close the loop 宣告收尾，接著自己提煉一個 takeaway 當結論。主持人替段落下結論，對話才有段落感；對方若不同意會補充，反而更好。
questions.pattern: Just to close the loop here, one takeaway here that I think is really interesting is that [X].
questions.episode: 35 years of product design wisdom from Apple, Disney, Pinterest, and beyond | Bob Baxley

questions.q: Anything else before we move on to number two?
questions.zh: 在進到第二點之前，還有什麼要補的嗎？
questions.why: 八個字完成一次收尾：確認補充＋標記進度。清單式的對話裡最好用，因為每次轉場都在提醒大家還剩幾點。
questions.pattern: Anything else before we move on to number [two]?
questions.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more
